mechanism: Map bar indices into each polynomial's domain (Legendre/Chebyshev/Laguerre/Hermite or hybrid Chebyshev-Hermite), apply discrete zero-sum correction for degrees≥1, then decompose the price window as a weighted sum of polynomials; weights of degree 0 recover SMA and higher degrees act as fixed-ratio oscillators. Use the fitted curve as smoother/trend and the weight vector as independent component features (up to degree N-1 for N prices).
data_needed: Close (or OHLC) window of length iPeriod≥degree+1; precomputed polynomial basis on shifted x; weight formula from article; optional feed of weight ratios into a downstream model.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MetaTrader 5 chart/_Symbol/_Period; demo strategies on price×polynomial and dual-polynomial crosses; degree 0–9, practical focus ≤3.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an orthogonal multi-component smoother/feature bank (noise-robust Legendre, edge-sensitive Chebyshev, recent-sensitive Laguerre, nonlinear Chebyshev-Hermite) rather than a single MA—each weight is an independent sensing channel.
quote: Any time series can be decomposed into a sum of polynomials taken with a certain weight

mechanism: Define volatility as std of percent returns over last 50 closed bars; z-score with training-set scaler_mean/scaler_std; fit 2-state GaussianHMM on scaled vol (high vs low). Online, maintain a 50-length scaled-vol ring buffer and run Viterbi with exported transition A, emission μ/σ², and π≈[0.5,0.5] to decode the current hidden state; gate trend-following MA-cross entries only when state==1 (high vol).
data_needed: Close series; rolling return std(50); StandardScaler mean/std; HMM transmat/means/covars; Viterbi DP tables T1/T2 over 50 obs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; train 2020-01-01→2024-01-01, OOS 2024→2025; rolling 4y-train/1y-test from 2004.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit unsupervised high/low volatility regime sensor with Markov transition structure and online Viterbi state decode—usable as a MIS regime/vol gate independent of the backbone signal.
quote: we will use Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to cluster volatility and define high and low volatility states

mechanism: Detect bullish/bearish order-block candle sequences, simulate OB entries to label each bar buy(1)/sell(-1)/hold(0), then train an LSTM on length-50 OHLC sequences to predict the next label (Dense tanh output in [-1,1]). Deploy via Python microservice + MQL5 WebRequest so the sequence model becomes a live buy/sell/hold sensor overlaid on the OB strategy.
data_needed: XAUUSD H1 OHLC CSV; order-block pattern labels; sequences of 50×4 OHLC; saved lstm_trading_model.h5; HTTP bridge for inference.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD H1; session hour filters Time1Hstrt/Time1Hend on the OB EA.
why_new_for_mis: Turns a rule-based structure detector into a supervised sequence sensor: LSTM learns temporal OHLC patterns tied to institutional OB events rather than static thresholds.
quote: We then trained the LSTM model on sequences of historical price data to predict whether the next market move should be a buy, sell, or hold

mechanism: Central Force Optimization metaheuristic for numerical search (probe masses from fitness, one-way gravitational attraction, kinematic updates, optional noise). Benchmarked on Hilly/Forest/Megacity test functions—no market regime, volatility, liquidity, or price-sequence sensor is built.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic AO test functions only; no traded instrument/timeframe sensing.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content after full read—optimizer implementation/rating only.
quote: The Central Force Optimization (CFO) algorithm is an attempt to transfer the principles of gravitational kinematics to the field of numerical optimization

mechanism: Python/tkinter/SQLite home-accounting GUI for manual income/expense/assets and MT5 report metric education (PF, Sharpe, drawdown). Mentions future ML forecasting only as a wishlist—no market sensing model is implemented.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic trader bookkeeping; example MT5 report from a 3D-bar system, not a sensing pipeline.
why_new_for_mis: Accounting/UI and capital-management pedagogy only; no regime/vol/liquidity/neural sensor after full read.
quote: Successful trading is impossible without clear financial accounting

mechanism: For each of 28 major FX pairs, compute percent close-vs-prior-open change on H1/H4/D1, then strength = 0.2·H1 + 0.3·H4 + 0.5·D1. Bubble-sort pairs by strength; surface top-10 strong and bottom-10 weak on a dashboard with color coding—basket-relative strength sensing à la Dalio group view.
data_needed: CopyRates for 28 pairs on PERIOD_H1/H4/D1 (2 bars each); timer refresh (default 60s); SPairStrength array.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD,GBPUSD,USDJPY,… full 28-pair list; H1+H4+D1 weighted; MetaTrader 5 separate-window panel.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-sectional multi-timeframe relative-strength sensor over a currency basket—answers whether a pair move is base-strong or quote-weak, which single-pair indicators miss.

mechanism: Fractal-Based Algorithm partitions search space into subspaces, ranks by density of top P1% fitness points, subdivides top P2% subspaces, regenerates population by rank, mutates via power-law around best. Pure continuous optimization benchmark—no market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing after full read—metaheuristic ranking article.
quote: This approach is based on the geometric properties of fractals and uses the concept of self-similarity to adaptively explore space

mechanism: On Darvas box breakout (price leaves confirmed high/low box), collect features (ADX, ADXWilder, DeMarker, RSI, RVI, Stochastic, 3 stationary open-close returns, box size, distance to box high/low) and label by whether equal % TP or SL hits first. Train CatBoostClassifier; at live breakout, predict_proba and trade the side whose confidence exceeds threshold (model generates direction, not merely filters a fixed side).
data_needed: Darvas detect (lookBack, checkBar); 12-feature vector; Excel deal profits merged to CSV; ONNX CatBoost; threshold (e.g. 0.7).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD M15; train/val 2020–2024, OOS 2024–2025; SL/TP as 0.3% of price.
why_new_for_mis: Supervised ML as the directional signal at a structure event (balanced TP/SL labels) rather than only as a binary filter on an already-sided backbone—larger sample space for MIS neural sensing.
quote: Essentially, we’re using the model to generate the buy or sell signals

mechanism: Map CatBoost class probability in (threshold,1] directly to position risk fraction via calclots(sl_distance, risk*prob)—optionally amplify separation with prob³—so sensed confidence continuously scales exposure instead of fixed lot discrete signals.
data_needed: predict_proba outputs; account balance; SL distance in price; SYMBOL tick size/value/volume step.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same XAUUSD M15 Darvas+CatBoost EA; OOS 2024–2025 comparison vs discrete.
why_new_for_mis: Treats model confidence as a continuous intensity sensor for risk, coupling neural output magnitude to sizing when accuracy rises with confidence.
quote: Continuous signals take this additive approach further, applying it to more abstract strategy conditions and producing a risk level between zero and one

mechanism: Train a second CatBoost on the same breakout labels but with features pulled from a higher TF (e.g. H1 indicators/returns, using bar shift 1 to avoid look-ahead). At M15 breakout, average the two models’ buy/sell probabilities and threshold the consensus (equal weights in article).
data_needed: Parallel feature getters on PERIOD_CURRENT and PERIOD_H1; two ONNX/CatBoost models; averaged probabilities.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XAUUSD; signal TF M15 with H1 feature model; same Darvas trigger.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-timeframe neural consensus as a confirmation sensor—reduces single-TF noise by requiring agreement of specialized models on one outcome.
quote: Training separate machine learning models, each using a different timeframe of features to predict the same outcome, can offer a powerful way to improve trade filtering and signal generation

mechanism: Smooth close with Savitzky–Golay (or SMA/EMA/spline), take np.gradient as trend, divide by rolling std(vol_window) to get normalized_trend; label Buy if >threshold, Sell if <−threshold, else no-signal. Optional variants keep only forward-profitable labels and/or OR signals across multiple rolling periods—volatility-scaled trend regime for supervised training.
data_needed: Close series; savgol_filter/rolling/EMA/spline; rolling std; threshold; optional markup/min_l/max_l and rolling_periods list.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train backward from 2000 with forward split 2024; CatBoost ONNX EA.
why_new_for_mis: Trend direction sensor that is explicitly normalized by local volatility so weak moves in quiet markets are suppressed—cleaner regime labels than raw slope.

mechanism: Cluster market into n_clusters regimes; train a primary CatBoost buy/sell model only on labeled trades inside each cluster. Meta-model learns cluster membership (trade-allowed vs not); when use_meta_dilution, dates labeled 2.0 (no trade) flip the meta target to 0 so the meta sensor jointly blocks wrong regimes and undesirable entry points.
data_needed: Feature clustering; per-cluster trend labels; meta_feature columns; dual CatBoost (main Accuracy, meta F1); ONNX export pair.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; n_clusters=10; periods list 5..300 step 30; SL 50 / TP 20 (4-digit points example).
why_new_for_mis: Second-stage neural regime gate that absorbs ‘no-trade’ labels instead of discarding them—MIS can sense both which cluster and whether entry is admissible.
quote: the second model will now predict both the required market regime and undesirable market entry points

mechanism: From the RTH session open bar, accumulate VWAP = Σ(typical_price×volume)/Σ(volume) with typical=(H+L+C)/3. Use close vs session VWAP as intraday trend-following entry filter and as a dynamic trailing exit when price crosses back through VWAP (strategies 2 and 3).
data_needed: Intraday OHLC+volume from session open index; getVWAP(startCandle); optional MA regime filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USTEC (Nasdaq-100 CFD); M15 for VWAP trend-follow, M1 for bands strategy; session ~18:30–24:00 broker UTC+2/3; backtest 2020–2025.
why_new_for_mis: Session-anchored volume-weighted fair-price sensor for MIS intraday liquidity/trend—resets daily and weights active traded prices, unlike global SMA.
quote: The intuition behind VWAP is to measure the average price a security trades at, weighted by volume, reflecting the "true" cost of trading over a period

mechanism: At clock time HH:MM, sigma = mean over past 14 days of |close_HHMM/open_0930 − 1|; upper = open_0930_today×(1+sigma), lower = open_0930_today×(1−sigma). Breakout of 1-minute bar through bands defines momentum beyond the historical same-time noise area—time-of-day volatility envelope sensing.
data_needed: M1 bars; today’s 9:30 open; for i=1..14 prior days’ 9:30 open and same HH:MM close; band cross detection.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USTEC M1; RTH 9:30 ET open; 14-day lookback; SL 1% + VWAP trail; 2020–2025.
why_new_for_mis: Intraday noise-range sensor conditioned on clock time (not rolling ATR alone)—MIS can flag moves that exceed typical open-to-now excursion for that minute of day.
quote: The strategy uses volatility-based bands, calculated from the previous day’s close or current day’s open and adjusted by a volatility multiplier, to define a "Noise Area"
